title: Span ordering and timestamp correction for robust Tempo ingestion
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem: We continue to see a class of reconstructed traces in Tempo where spans arrive out-of-order or with skewed timestamps from heterogeneous clients (mobile SDKs, legacy Jaeger bridges, async workers). These result in inaccurate latency percentiles on UI dashboards and noisy error-aggregation. Goal: Implement a resilient ingestion-side pipeline that corrects common timestamp skew patterns, aligns span batches for out-of-order arrival, and emits provenance markers so downstream Tempo/Querier can reconstruct accurate spans without dropping fidelity. This is an ingestion-focused change (collector-side) and must be safe for hosted and dedicated environments.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Incoming OTLP/Jaeger spans with clock skew < 5s are adjusted deterministically and retain original timestamp in an attribute. 2) Out-of-order spans within a 10s window are coalesced into aligned batches and forwarded to Tempo with preserved causal ordering metadata. 3) Any span with >30s skew is flagged and forwarded unchanged plus an alert metric. 4) End-to-end latency dashboards show reduced high-p99 artifacts on synthetic workload (>=30% reduction on previous test harness). 5) Feature toggle behind runtime flag; can be rolled back without data loss.
design_notes: - Strategy: lightweight timestamp correction heuristics + a bounded reordering buffer per trace id. Use a configurable window (default 10s) to hold early-arriving spans and sort by event time before emitting. - Preserve original timestamps in span attribute: "original.event_time" and add "redwood.ingest.adjusted" boolean. - Mark spans that were reordered with "redwood.ingest.ordering_hint": values {"in-order","reordered","skipped"}. - For legacy Jaeger envelopes: map jaeger.timestamp to otlp.time_unix_ns and run same correction path. - Avoid unbounded memory by capping buffer size per trace and evict policy (oldest or highest latency). - Emit metrics: ingest.reordering.count, ingest.skew.flagged, ingest.buffer.evictions, ingest.processing.latency. - Runtime flags: enable_ingest_correction, reorder_window_ms, max_buffer_spans, skew_threshold_ms. - Security: no PII added; original timestamps stored only as numeric attributes.
implementation_plan: 1) Prototype: implement per-trace ring-buffer + sort routine inside collector and run locally with synthetic producers (2 days). 2) Instrument metrics and create dashboard (2 days). 3) Bench tests: throughput/regressions with 1M spans/min (3 days). 4) Implement feature toggle + config passthrough for Dedicated/Private (2 days). 5) Staged rollout: canary on non-critical tenant slice -> expand -> all-hosted. 6) Post-rollout verification: A/B dashboard comparison and sampling reconciliation (2 days).
rollout_plan: - Phase 0: Deploy to staging cluster with feature off. - Phase 1: Canary with feature on for synthetic tenant group (10% traffic) for 48h. Monitor ingest.processing.latency and buffer.evictions. - Phase 2: Gradual ramp to 50% over 72h if stable. - Phase 3: Full fleet rollout. - Rollback: flip enable_ingest_correction=false; collectors will emit spans unchanged. Ensure dashboards have baseline snapshots to compare.
monitoring_and_metrics: Track: ingest.reordering.count (per-tenant), ingest.skew.flagged (per-region), ingest.buffer.evictions, ingest.processing.latency_ms p50/p95/p99, tempo.ingest.write.latency, dashboards: trace-latency-p99-by-service. Add alerts: >0.1% of traces flagged for >30s skew for >1h OR buffer_evictions rate increase > 2x baseline.
risks_and_mitigation: - Risk: Reordering buffer adds latency to tail; mitigation: bounded window, per-tenant limits, and circuit-breaker that disables correction under high load. - Risk: Memory pressure in high-cardinality traces; mitigation: cap buffer size and evict oldest spans, emit metric + sample evicted traces for debugging. - Risk: Breaking downstream expectations for strict chronological ordering; mitigation: keep original timestamps as attributes and do not rewrite trace ids or span ids.
